While playing for [[Indiana University–Purdue University Indianapolis]] (IUPUI), he was named [[Summit League Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Summit League Player of the Year]] and was an honorable mention [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] in his junior season. A guard, Hill was selected 26th overall by the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in the [[2008 NBA draft]]. He spent three seasons with the team before being traded to the [[Indiana Pacers]] in June 2011. He spent five seasons in Indiana and was dealt to the [[Utah Jazz draft history|Utah Jazz]] in July 2016. Hill has also played for the [[Sacramento Kings]], the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], and the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. He played in the [[2018 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] as a member of the Cavaliers in 2018. ==Early life== Born and raised in [[Indianapolis, Indiana]], Hill looked up to players like [[Michael Jordan]], [[Magic Johnson]], and [[Larry Bird]] while dreaming of one day playing in the NBA; when asked about his goal of becoming a first-round pick in the [[2008 NBA draft]], Hill commented: "It's my childhood dream".Matt Baker. [http://www.indystar.com/apps/pbcs.dll/article?AID=/20080626/SPORTS/806260437/1088/SPORTS04 IUPUI's George Hill dreams of having his name called]''indystar.com'', June 26, 2008. - He played basketball at St. Richard's Episcopal School. An only child,Maurice M. McKiernan. [http://media.www.jagbytes.com/media/storage/paper1244/news/2008/02/20/Sports/Iupuis.George.Hill.The.Man.Behind.The.Stats-3221934.shtml IUPUI's George Hill: the man behind the stats] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090220141025/http://media.www.jagbytes.com/media/storage/paper1244/news/2008/02/20/Sports/Iupuis.George.Hill.The.Man.Behind.The.Stats-3221934.shtml |date=February 20, 2009 }} ''jagbytes.com'', February 20, 2008. – [https://web.archive.org/web/20220613001910/http://www.jagbytes.com/home/index.cfm?event=displayArticlePrinterFriendly&uStory_id=7107c39d-c289-4f9b-bdd5-442184c56b1b Archived at WebCite] Hill attended [[Broad Ripple High School]]Indianapolis Public Schools. [http://www.headlines.ips.k12.in.us/archive/7118.aspx 2004 BRHS Graduate Hill Picked in First Round of NBA Draft] ''headlines.ips.k12.in.us'' – [https://web.archive.org/web/20111004180647/http://www.headlines.ips.k12.in.us/archive/7118.aspx Archived at WebCite] where he excelled as one of the top high school players in the state and was one of the "Magnificent Seven" from Indianapolis (with [[Greg Oden]], [[Mike Conley Jr.]], [[Josh McRoberts]], [[Rodney Carney]], [[Eric Gordon]], and [[Courtney Lee]]).Rabjohns, Jeff. [http://iw.newsbank.com/iw-search/we/InfoWeb?p_action=doc&p_theme=aggdocs&p_topdoc=1&p_docnum=1&p_sort=YMD_date:D&p_product=AWNB&p_docid=1241CDA351F36DB0&p_text_direct-0=document_id=(%201241CDA351F36DB0%20)&p_nbid=C5FQ62WWMTIyNjE2MDY0OC4zOTgwNzk6MToxMToxMjkuMTE1LjAuMA "Magnificent Seven – Oden. Conley. McRoberts. Carney. Hill. Lee. And Gordon. Indy high school rivals, now NBA colleagues, take us back to beginning. They recall classic games back in high school – and even elementary school"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100809145945/http://iw.newsbank.com/iw-search/we/InfoWeb?p_action=doc |date=August 9, 2010 }}, Indianapolis Star, The (IN). Final Edition, Sports, D01. (ind138231025) Carney remembers playing against Hill: "This little kid comes in hitting all kinds of 3s, and I was like, 'Who is this little dude?...I knew he was going to be something when I saw this little skinny kid handling the ball and shooting like that." Hill played against every member of the Magnificent Seven except Gordon, who was recovering from a broken wrist during their meetup. He faced off against Oden and Conley during his junior year in high school, and remembers playing [[Streetball|pickup games]] against 10-year-old Gordon when he was 13. In his senior year, Hill averaged a state-leading 36.2 points per game, the fifth-highest single-season average in [[Indiana High School Athletic Association]] history.[http://www.iupuijags.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=7 2007–2008 Men's Basketball Roster] ''iupuijags.com''. – [https://web.archive.org/web/20080802072454/http://www.iupuijags.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=7 Archived at Webcite] ==College career== Despite scholarship offers from several big conference schools, including [[Temple University|Temple]] and [[Indiana University|Indiana]], he chose to commit to [[Indiana University-Purdue University Indianapolis|IUPUI]], wishing to stay with his ailing great-grandfather, Gilbert Edison.[http://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/MYSA062808_4D_BKNspurs_hill_3feba72_html.html Hill a prototypical Spur: College coach recounts examples of toughness, talent, loyalty, desire] ''mysanantonio.com'' June 27, 2008 – [https://web.archive.org/web/20080730044805/http://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/MYSA062808_4D_BKNspurs_hill_3feba72_html.html Archived at WebCite] A few months after he agreed to attend IUPUI, his great-grandfather died, never getting the opportunity to see Hill play basketball at the college level. Following his great-grandfather's advice to always be a man of his word, Hill decided to pass on other offers and stay at IUPUI. In his sophomore year, he led the [[IUPUI Jaguars]] to a tie for the best record in the conference. Following an injury that forced him to become a [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]] in his third year at IUPUI, Hill returned the next season and led the Jaguars to a school-record 26 wins and the Summit League Tournament finals before losing to eventual champion [[Oral Roberts University]] and thus failing to secure a spot in the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA]] tournament. Not counting Hill's injury-shortened 2006–07 season, the Jaguars were 61–30 during his three seasons at IUPUI. Despite having one year of eligibility left, Hill, wishing to "test the waters", declared himself eligible for the [[2008 NBA draft]]. He left IUPUI as the fifth all-time leading scorer with 1,619 points, and became the second IUPUI player to declare early"IUPUI's Hill declares for NBA draft", The Associated Press State & Local Wire. May 1, 2008. after Carlos Knox in 1997 (he later withdrew his name). ==Professional career== === San Antonio Spurs (2008–2011) === Although he had regularly attracted NBA scouts to his college games, Hill was not projected in most mock drafts largely due to remaining unannounced.Jeff Rabjohns (May 1, 2008). "IUPUI's Hill to test his NBA value". ''Indianapolis Star'', The (IN) FINAL EDITION ed., D02. Retrieved November 6, 2008 from NewsBank on-line database (Access World News) on the World Wide Web: <[http://infoweb.newsbank.com infoweb.newsbank.com]>. (ID: ind131429991) {{blockquote|text=The hard part was putting my name in, knowing I have great teammates and great coaches and if it came down to me leaving, I wouldn't be able to play for the team or the coaches again...The easy thing was, if I put my name in and don't get drafted, I still have the option of coming back and playing for this great university. |sign=George Hill |source= |}} In the following months, Hill worked out with several NBA teams. After an impressive run at the Orlando pre-draft rookie camp, Hill attracted attention and became a projected second-round selection. On draft night, the [[San Antonio Spurs]] surprised many by selecting Hill with their 26th pick in the first round; many expected the Spurs to select [[Mario Chalmers]] of [[University of Kansas|Kansas]].Wallace, Michael. [http://www.miamiherald.com/sports/basketball/story/762351.html "Miami Heat's Chalmers feels at home in San Antonio"], The Miami Herald. November 8, 2008. Hill became the second first-round draft choice in [[The Summit League]]'s history and the first player ever drafted from [[Indiana University-Purdue University Indianapolis|IUPUI]].Ed Holdaway. [http://www.iupuijags.com/news/2008/6/26/MBB_0626085013.aspx "Hill picked 26th overall by the San Antonio Spurs"] ''iupuijags.com'', June 25, 2006. Accessed July 12, 2008. – [https://web.archive.org/web/20080727124154/http://www.iupuijags.com/news/2008/6/26/MBB_0626085013.aspx Archived at WebCite] On September 23, 2008, the Spurs signed Hill to a standard rookie contract that guaranteed the first two years and included a team option on the next two years.Cliff Brunt, [https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/news?slug=ap-spurs-hill&prov=ap&type=lgns Spurs sign George Hill] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100213171648/http://sports.yahoo.com/nba/news?slug=ap-spurs-hill&prov=ap&type=lgns |date=February 13, 2010 }} ''sports.yahoo.com,'' September 23, 2008. ==== 2008–09 season ==== On July 14, 2008, in his first summer league game as a Spur, Hill scored 17 points and grabbed 8 rebounds while holding fellow draft pick [[O. J. Mayo]] to 5-of-17 shooting en route to a victory for the Spurs.Mike Monroe. [http://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/spurs/Spurs-Hill-holds-own-against-Mayo.html Spurs' Hill holds own against Mayo in summer league debut] ''mysanantonio.com'', July 15, 2008. – {{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20080730064002/http://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/spurs/Spurs-Hill-holds-own-against-Mayo.html|title=Archived at WebCite}} Throughout the summer league Hill struggled with his shooting, making only 2 of 25 shots (8.0%), and one of six three-pointers (16.7%). Hill played in all but one of the four summer league games for the Spurs; he finished averaging 8.0 points, 7.0 rebounds, and 3.0 assists in 31.7 minutes per game.[http://www.nba.com/summerleague2008/players/index.jsp?player=george_hill George Hill (2008 Summer League Statistics)] ''nba.com'', Accessed July 21, 2008. – [https://web.archive.org/web/20080727190753/http://www.nba.com/summerleague2008/players/index.jsp?player=george_hill Archived at WebCite]Mike Monroe. [http://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/spurs/Spurs_Hill_makes_date_to_fix_his_wayward_shot.html Spurs' Hill makes date to fix his wayward shot] ''mysanantonio.com'', July 17, 2008. Accessed July 21, 2008. – [https://web.archive.org/web/20080727052101/http://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/spurs/Spurs_Hill_makes_date_to_fix_his_wayward_shot.html Archived at WebCite] At the Utah Revue, Hill led his team by averaging 12.9 points over four games; however he continued to struggle offensively with his shooting, only making 21.4% of his three-point field goals.Tim Buckley. [https://www.espn.com/espn/print?id=3505958&type=story Warriors' Morrow named MVP of the Revue] ''espn.com'', July 26, 2008. – [https://www.espn.com/espn/print?id=3505958&type=story Archived at WebCite] In the first of the four games, Hill led all scorers with 21 points and helped the Spurs defeat the [[Utah Jazz]], 82–57. He followed up with a quiet offensive performance, 6 points, in a win against the [[NBDL]] Ambassadors, before scoring 18 points in a loss versus the [[Gerald Green]]-led [[Dallas Mavericks|Mavericks]]. In the final game of the Revue, Hill once again struggled with his shooting (1–7) but managed to make key plays with the game on the line. Hill made two clutch free throws with 6.9 seconds left and then forced a turnover on the defensive end to beat the previously undefeated [[Atlanta Hawks]].[http://www.nba.com/jazz/Revue/rmr2008_schedule.html "2008 RMR Schedule"] ''nba.com/jazz/Renue'', July 18 – 25.[http://www.nba.com/jazz/Revue/rmr2008_day4_atlsas.html "08 RMR Day 4: Atlanta vs. San Antonio"] ''nba.com/jazz/Revue'', July 22, 2008. In 2008, Hill joined the [[San Antonio Spurs]] and made his NBA debut on November 4 against the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in the third game of the season. He had sat out the previous two games due to a sprained left thumb.Finger, Mike. [http://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/columnists/mike_finger/This_time_Hill_prepared_to_answer_call.html This time, Hill prepared to answer call] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081108022015/http://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/columnists/mike_finger/This_time_Hill_prepared_to_answer_call.html |date=November 8, 2008 }}, ''Mysanantonio.com'', November 5, 2008. In 15 minutes of play, Hill finished with 11 points, 1 steal, and 1 assist.[http://www.nba.com/games/20081104/DALSAS/boxscore.html NBA Mavericks at Spurs Boxscore] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121105021554/http://www.nba.com/games/20081104/DALSAS/boxscore.html |date=November 5, 2012 }}, ''NBA.com'', November 4, 2008. Hill initially served as the main reserve at point guard, but after [[Tony Parker]] suffered an injury early in the season he was promoted to starter.[https://web.archive.org/web/20160304064135/http://news.xinhuanet.com/english/2008-11/11/content_10341584.htm " Spurs' Parker out one month for ankle sprain "], ''China View (xinhuanet.com)'' November 11, 2008.[http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2008/basketball/nba/11/07/Parker.injury.ap/index.html "Parker injured early in game"]{{dead link|date=September 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}, ''Sports Illustrated'' November 7, 2008. After the return of Parker and Manu Ginóbili, Hill received fewer minutes.Monroe, Mike. [http://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/spurs/Late_surge_propels_Spurs_past_Rockets.html "Late surge propels Spurs past Rockets"] {{Dead link|date=December 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}, San Antonio Express News. November 14, 2008. (Accessed November 15, 2008)San Antonio(AP).[http://www.nba.com/spurs/gameday/081114.html "Duncan scores 22 points, leads the Spurs to another home victory"], NBA.com, November 14, 2008 He finished his rookie season averaging 5.7 points per game, 2.1 rebounds per game, and 1.8 assists per game. Hill made his playoff debut in game 2 of the Spurs first-round series against the Mavs, but only played 5 minutes.{{Cite web |title=George Hill Career Stats - NBA |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/stats/_/id/3438/george-hill |access-date=2024-02-20 |website=ESPN |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=George Hill 2008-09 Stats per Game - NBA |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3438/year/2009 |access-date=2024-02-20 |website=ESPN |language=en}} ====2009–10 season==== [[File:Jameer Nelson and George Hill.jpg|thumb|right|Hill in March 2010, defending [[Jameer Nelson]] of the [[Orlando Magic]]]] Hill spent most of his off-season working on his point-guard skills, supervised by player development coach Chad Forcier, and his jump shots with Spurs shooting coach Chip Engelland. Following the advice of former Spur [[Bruce Bowen]], he focused on developing his corner three-point shot. By the time training camp arrived, Hill had converted 8,000 threes. His hard work during the off-season paid large dividends as soon as the 2009–10 season commenced. Hill saw his minutes increase from 16.5 to 29 a game. He also started in 43 games, most of them while Tony Parker was battling injuries. Hill more than doubled his scoring average, improved his field goal percentage by 7.5 percentage points, and his 3-pt shooting by 7.9 percentage points. On April 1, Hill notched career highs of 30 points, 5 steals, and 7 assists in a home game win against the Houston Rockets.McDonald, Jeff [http://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/spurs/Hill_leads_Spurs_past_Rockets.html?c=y&page=2#storytop "Hill leads Spurs past Rockets"] MySA.com, April 1, 2010. Hill ended the regular season tied at second place with [[Kevin Durant]] and Marc Gasol for the Most Improved Player of the Year award. All three garnered a total of 101 points.Duncan, Chris [https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/news?slug=ap-brooks-mostimproved "Rockets G Brooks NBA's most improved player"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100426135603/http://sports.yahoo.com/nba/news?slug=ap-brooks-mostimproved |date=April 26, 2010 }} Yahoo! Sports, April 22, 2010 The Spurs' first-round playoff series with the Mavs was a breakout series for Hill. He was ineffective in Game 1, scoring 0 points in 17 minutes after coming back from an ankle injury. He shook off his tentativeness in the next few games, scoring 7 and 17 points in Games 2 and 3. Then Hill led the Spurs to a Game 4 victory on a night when the Spurs' Big Three of Duncan, Parker, and Ginobili shot a combined 9-of-34 from the field. Hill scored a career playoff high 29 points, shooting 11–16 from the field and 5–6 from 3-point range.{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130209205904/http://sports.yahoo.com/nba/boxscore;_ylt=AjEqWg4G9LHq9UeHJQtoCAvlPaB4?gid=2010042524|title="Spurs vs. Mavs, Game 4 boxscore"}} Yahoo! Sports Hill averaged 22.3 points in the series, helping the Spurs to win the series in six games. ====2010–11 season==== [[File:GHill against Celtics.JPG|thumb|right|150px|Hill in March 2011]] On March 28, 2011, Hill matched his career high of 30 points in a 119–114 loss to the [[Houston Rockets]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20110327/SASMEM/gameinfo.html |title=Spurs-Grizzlies notebook |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=April 5, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110128153255/http://www.nba.com/games/20110327/SASMEM/gameinfo.html |archive-date=January 28, 2011 |url-status=dead }} ===Indiana Pacers (2011–2016)=== Hill was traded to his hometown team the [[Indiana Pacers]] during the [[2011 NBA Draft|2011 NBA draft]] on June 23, 2011, a trade that sent rights to the 15th overall pick [[Kawhi Leonard]], the 42nd pick, [[Dāvis Bertāns]], and 2005 draftee [[Erazem Lorbek]] to the Spurs in exchange for Hill.[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=6698432 Pacers acquire guard George Hill] Hill started the shortened season as a backup for [[Darren Collison]]. On January 31, 2012, Hill left the game against the [[New Jersey Nets]] after suffering an ankle injury. The Pacers announced it was a small chip fracture.[https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2012/2/1/2763565/george-hill-injury-ankle-indiana-pacers George Hill Injury: Pacers Guard Out Indefinitely With Chip Fracture In Ankle] He missed 12 games with the injury and returned on February 22, against the [[Charlotte Bobcats]]. On April 9, 2012, Pacers coach [[Frank Vogel]] announced that Hill would start for the injured Collison. Although Collison returned from the injury, Hill remained a starter for the rest of the season. Hill finished the season averaging 9.6 points per game with a field goal percentage of .442. During their first-round playoff series against the [[Orlando Magic]], Hill scored double-digits in all five games as the Pacers advanced to the Eastern Conferences Semifinal. Facing the [[Miami Heat]] in the Conference Semifinals, Hill scored a playoff high 20 points and 5 assists in game 3. The Heat won the next 3 games, advancing to the Conference Finals and eventually becoming NBA champions. On July 13, 2012, Hill re-signed with the Pacers to a reported five-year, $40 million contract.{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=10496 |title=Pacers re-sign Roy Hibbert, George Hill |access-date=November 15, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180711091346/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=10496 |archive-date=July 11, 2018 |url-status=dead }} Hill became the full-time starter after the departure of Darren Collison, who would be traded to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] for [[Ian Mahinmi]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/mavericks-sign-and-trade-ian-mahinmi-for-darren-collison-and-dahntay-jones/ |title=Mavericks sign-and-trade Ian Mahinmi for Darren Collison and Dahntay Jones |access-date=June 23, 2026}} [[File:George Hill Pacers.jpg|left|Hill with the Pacers in March 2014|upright|thumb]] During the 2012–13 season, Hill made a game-winning floater against the [[Toronto Raptors]] and a game-winning layup over the outstretched arms of [[Dwight Howard]] against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. Hill and the Pacers appeared in the Eastern Conference Finals, but lost to the defending champion [[2012-13 Miami Heat season|Miami Heat]] in 7 games. Hill perhaps had the best game of his NBA career on February 7, 2014, when he scored a career-high 37 points in a win against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] along with 9 rebounds and 8 assists including a game-tying three-pointer to force the game to overtime.[https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2014/02/07/george-hill-scores-37-as-pacers-win-118-113-in-overtime/5300205/ George Hill scores 37 as Pacers win 118–113 in overtime] After missing the first 28 games of the season with a left knee injury, Hill returned to action on December 23 against the New Orleans Pelicans. In just over 21 minutes of action off the bench, he recorded 15 points, 4 rebounds, 3 assists and 1 steal in the 96–84 win.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141223/NOPIND/gameinfo.html |title=Hill leads Pacers over Pelicans 96–84 |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=January 1, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180712124316/http://www.nba.com/games/20141223/NOPIND/gameinfo.html |archive-date=July 12, 2018 |url-status=dead }} On February 27, 2015, Hill recorded his first career triple-double with 15 points, 10 rebounds and 12 assists in a 93–86 win over the Cleveland Cavaliers.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150227/CLEIND/gameinfo.html |title=Surging Pacers hold off short-handed Cavaliers 93–86 |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=February 28, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180712124609/http://www.nba.com/games/20150227/CLEIND/gameinfo.html |archive-date=July 12, 2018 |url-status=dead }} On March 14, he scored a season-high 30 points in an 89–93 loss to the Boston Celtics.[https://www.nba.com/games/20150314/BOSIND/gameinfo.html Celtics take control early, then hold off Pacers 93–89] On February 19, 2016, Hill had nine points and nine assists and matched a career-high with 11 rebounds in the Pacers' 101–98 win over the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160219/INDOKC/gameinfo.html |title=Ellis scores 27 as Pacers beat Thunder 101–98 |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=February 21, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160222020513/http://www.nba.com/games/20160219/INDOKC/gameinfo.html |archive-date=February 22, 2016 |url-status=dead }} ===Utah Jazz (2016–2017)=== On July 7, 2016, Hill was traded to the [[Utah Jazz]] in a three-team deal involving the Pacers and the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-acquire-george-hill-indiana|title=Jazz Acquire George Hill from Indiana|work=NBA.com|date=July 7, 2016|access-date=July 7, 2016}} He made his debut for the Jazz in their season opener on October 25 against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], recording 19 points and six assists in a 113–104 loss.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899376|title=Lillard scores 39, Blazers run home-opening win streak to 16|work=ESPN.com|date=October 26, 2016|access-date=October 26, 2016}} On November 7, he was named Western Conference Player of the Week for games played Monday, October 31 through Sunday, November 6. Hill helped the Jazz to a 3–1 week behind averages of 20.8 points, 5.8 assists and 3.3 rebounds.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/article/2016/11/07/players-week-lebron-james-george-hill|title=LeBron James, George Hill named NBA Players of the Week|work=NBA.com|date=November 7, 2016|access-date=November 7, 2016}} On November 23, he scored 22 points in his return from an eight-game absence, as the Jazz snapped a four-game losing streak with a 108–83 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899671|title=Hill scores 22 in return, Jazz beat Nuggets 108–83|work=ESPN.com|date=November 23, 2016|access-date=November 24, 2016}} On December 29, he returned to action against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] after missing 13 games with a sprained toe.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899931|title=Hill scores 21 in return, Jazz top 76ers 100–83 with big 4th|work=ESPN.com|date=December 29, 2016|access-date=December 29, 2016}} On January 21, 2017, he scored a season-high 30 points in a 109–100 win over the Pacers.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900080|title=Hill scores 30 vs. former team as Jazz beat Pacers 109–100|work=ESPN.com|date=January 21, 2017|access-date=January 22, 2017}} On March 3, 2017, he set a new season high with 34 points in a 112–97 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900310|title=Hill scores 34, Jazz beat Nets 112–97 in wire-to-wire win|work=ESPN.com|date=March 3, 2017|access-date=March 4, 2017}} ===Sacramento Kings (2017–2018)=== On July 10, 2017, Hill signed a three-year deal worth a reported $57 million with the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-george-hill|title=Kings Sign George Hill|work=NBA.com|date=July 10, 2017|access-date=July 10, 2017}} The deal was fully guaranteed for its first two seasons, with only $1 million guaranteed for the 2019–20 season.{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/22369379/cleveland-cavaliers-acquire-rodney-hood-george-hill-3-team-trade-utah-jazz-sacramento-kings|title=Cleveland Cavaliers acquire Rodney Hood, George Hill in 3-team trade with Utah Jazz, Sacramento Kings|work=[[ESPN.com]]|access-date=June 5, 2018}} ===Cleveland Cavaliers (2018)=== On February 8, 2018, Hill was acquired by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] in a three-team trade that also involved the Kings and the [[Utah Jazz]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/cavaliers/releases/rhood-ghill-trade-180208|title=Cavaliers Acquire George Hill and Rodney Hood in Three-Team Trade|work=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2018|access-date=February 8, 2018}} The Cavaliers made their 4th straight Finals appearance this season. In Game 1, Hill missed a game winning free throw attempt in regulation. Teammate [[J. R. Smith]] got Hill's free-throw rebound with 4.7 seconds left in regulation time. The game was tied, meaning that a field goal would have won the game. Smith, apparently confused and, thinking the Cavaliers were winning, attempted to dribble out the clock before realizing his error and frantically passing to Hill with 1.2 seconds left, in front of a visibly irate{{Cite web |last=Young |first=Ryan |date=2019-10-25 |title=J.R. Smith on his infamous 2018 NBA Finals mistake: 'I laughed about that s--t that night' |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba-finals-cleveland-cavaliers-jr-smith-game-1-mistake-lebron-james-golden-state-warriors-230817870.html |access-date=2026-03-05 |website=Yahoo Sports |language=en-US}} [[LeBron James]]. The Cavaliers lost 124–114 in overtime,{{Cite web |title=Warriors 124-114 Cavaliers (1 Jun, 2018) Game Recap |url=https://africa.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401034613 |access-date=2026-03-05 |website=ESPN |language=en}} and eventually lost the Finals in four games to the defending champion [[Golden State Warriors]].{{Cite web |date=2018-06-09 |title=2018 NBA Finals: Warriors sweep Cavaliers in four games for third title in four seasons |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/2018-nba-finals-warriors-sweep-cavaliers-in-four-games-for-third-title-in-four-seasons/ |access-date=2026-03-05 |website=CBS Sports |language=en}} ===Milwaukee Bucks (2018–2020)=== On December 7, 2018, Hill was traded to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] in a five-player, three-team deal that also included the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite news|title=Bucks Acquire George Hill and Jason Smith in a Three-Team Deal With Cleveland and Washington|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-acquire-george-hill-and-jason-smith-three-team-deal-cleveland-and-washington|access-date=December 8, 2018|work=NBA.com|date=December 7, 2018}} Hill and the Bucks appeared in the Eastern Conference Finals (the franchise's first since [[2000-01 Milwaukee Bucks season|2000–01]]), but were defeated in 6 games by the eventual champion [[2018-19 Toronto Raptors season|Toronto Raptors]]. Following the 2019 season, Hill signed a 3-year, $29 million contract to remain with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.spotrac.com/nba/milwaukee-bucks/george-hill-6154/|title=George Hill|last=Spotrac.com|website=Spotrac.com|language=en-US|access-date=2019-07-10}} On October 28, 2019, Hill scored 19 points and grabbed 8 rebounds in a 129–112 win over his former team, the Cavaliers.{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/201910280MIL.html|title=Cavaliers vs Bucks, October 28, 2019}} In his first full season with the Bucks in 2019–20, he led the NBA in three-point field goal percentage. Hill was integral in organizing a [[2020 American athlete strikes|wildcat strike]] of players during the 2020 [[2020 NBA Bubble|NBA bubble]] in response to the [[shooting of Jacob Blake]] and other instances of [[George Floyd protests|police violence]].{{Cite magazine|date=2020-08-27|title=The Exhilarating Jolt of the Milwaukee Bucks' Wildcat Strike|url=https://www.newyorker.com/sports/sporting-scene/the-exhilarating-jolt-of-the-milwaukee-bucks-wildcat-strike|access-date=2021-07-21|magazine=The New Yorker|language=en-US}} Despite finishing with the best record in the Eastern Conference at 56–17, the Bucks were defeated in the NBA Bubble during the Conference Semifinals by the 5th seeded [[2019-20 Miami Heat season|Miami Heat]] in 5 games. ===Oklahoma City Thunder (2020–2021)=== On November 24, 2020, Hill was traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in a four team deal also involving the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] and [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/hill-cheatham-gray-miller-williams-201124|title=Thunder Acquires George Hill, Zylan Cheatham, Josh Gray, Darius Miller, Kenrich Williams, One First and Two Second-Round Draft Picks and a Trade Exception|work=NBA.com|date=November 24, 2020}} On January 24, 2021, Hill fractured his right thumb in what would be his last game for the Thunder, and eventually underwent surgery.{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/30821750/oklahoma-city-thunder-george-hill-miss-least-4-weeks-thumb-procedure|title = Thunder's Hill (Thumb) to miss game against the [[Detroit Pistons]], and was ruled out indefinitely.[https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/nba/bucks/2022/04/25/milwaukee-bucks-injury-updates-khris-middleton-george-hill/7437872001/ day]], [[ESPN]] reported that Hill had a 6'9" [[wingspan]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/columns/story?columnist=thorpe_david&page=Rookies-081210 |title=Rookie Watch: Welcome, Westbrook Buckley. couple's first child, Zayden Jaxon Hill.[http://www.indycornrows.com/2016/1/21/10810854/george-hill-to-return-to-pacers-after-birth-of-his-son George Hill to return to Pacers after birth of his son] Hill owns an 850-acre ranch in Texas Hill Country, a 35-minute drive north of his offseason home in San Antonio. He employs 16 ranch workers to tend to the big herbivores he houses on his ranch.
